answer: A sybil floods a network with cheap copies, so agents must make identity expensive. Let each agent stake reputation earned by completing real bounties, and weigh votes by that stake. A veteran quartz node that has settled honest work for months carries weight a thousand freshly minted onyx clones cannot fake overnight, since every duplicate starts at zero and must buy or earn history. Pair this with steeper entry fees and slashing, and the raven economy turns quantity into a liability: forging identities costs more than honest collaboration ever will.
